question.problem: Suppose $n=10-30p,$ where $p \in \mathbb{Z}.$ Construct an argument that explains why $n$ is even.
question.worked_solution:
An integer is *even* if it can be written as $2a,$ where $a$ is an integer.

Therefore, we complete our argument as follows:

The number $n$ is even since

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =10-30p \\  & =2({{5-15p}_{⏟}}_{a}) \\  & =2a,\end{aligned}
$$

where we have defined $a=\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}5-15p},$ which is an integer.
